description: Local-profile checkpoint selection. The pipeline reads active_producer/active_auditor and maps every local_producer agent to the producer id and every local_auditor agent to the auditor id. If this file is absent or unreadable, the pipeline falls back to the original full-precision ids, so removing it restores the pre-existing behaviour exactly.
why: Quantising a full-precision checkpoint on the fly stages every fp16 shard in system RAM before writing 4-bit weights, so peak host RAM tracks the fp16 size (~15.2 GB for the 7B producer, ~7.6 GB for the auditor) rather than the ~5.5 GB / ~2.3 GB the weights finally occupy. On a 16 GB machine that peak is what kills the run. A pre-quantised checkpoint is read at its stored 4-bit size with no fp16 staging step. Same model family, same LAW-III producer/auditor split, same 4-bit NF4 weights.
notes: LAW-III: producer and auditor MUST stay in different model families (Qwen vs Phi). Changing active_producer/active_auditor to the full_precision ids restores the original load path, including its BitsAndBytesConfig quantise-on-load behaviour.
